questions.question: What is a class?

options.value: A definition of the state and behavior of its objects

questions.explanation: A class defines a type and the operations its instances support.

questions.question: What is an object?
questions.explanation: An object is a particular instance with its own identity and state.

questions.question: Which describes object state?

options.value: Values stored in its instance variables

questions.explanation: Instance fields hold information describing the object.

questions.question: Which describes object behavior?

options.value: Only the spelling of its variable name

questions.explanation: Methods implement actions or observations associated with objects.

questions.question: Two Counter objects are constructed separately. Must their counts always match?

options.value: No, each can have independent instance state
Yes, because the class is shared
Yes, because Java copies every update
Only if both references are local

questions.explanation: Separate objects normally have separate instance-field storage.

questions.question: A variable declared Counter c stores what?

options.value: A reference to a Counter object or null

questions.explanation: Reference variables identify objects rather than directly storing all object fields.

questions.question: What does null mean for a reference variable?

options.value: It is a new object with zero fields

questions.explanation: A null reference cannot act as the receiver of an instance-method call.

questions.question: What happens when an instance method is called through null?
questions.explanation: There is no receiver object on which to invoke the method.

questions.question: Two separately created Counter objects happen to have equal field values. What is still true?

options.value: They must be the same object

questions.explanation: Equal state does not imply identical object identity.

questions.question: Given Counter a = new Counter(); and Counter b = a;, what is the relationship?

options.value: a and b refer to the same object
b is automatically a deep copy

questions.explanation: Reference assignment copies the reference, creating an alias.
